name: pon_fiber_cut
description: A fibre cut on the span between two GPON OLTs, the ONU storm behind it, and the clears on repair. Two hosts with distinct addresses, driven live: `python testbed/control.py cut`, then `... repair`.
notes: THE SPAN uses the IETF standard linkDown (1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3) and linkUp (1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4) notifications from RFC 3418 / RFC 2863. The appliance carries that pair in known_oids.CLEAR_PAIR_SEEDS, so the span alarm clears on the FIRST repair with zero configuration.

THE ONUs use a vendor arc, and their raise/clear pairing is NOT bundled. The appliance learns it from strict alternation: learn.CLEAR_CYCLES_TO_LEARN = 2, so after cut/repair twice the pair is trusted and from the THIRD cut the ONU alarms clear too. That progression is the product's own thesis — the network teaches the appliance — and the lab is where you watch it happen.

Trap OIDs below an ENTERPRISE arc are ILLUSTRATIVE, not vendor-attested. The enterprise numbers are real IANA PENs (2011 Huawei, 1271 Ciena); the sub-arcs are shaped like a GPON/transport MIB and are not read from one. No vendor MIB file is in this repository. Attested vendor mappings with citations are v0.17.1's job.

THE SEVERITY VARBIND is X.733 perceived severity carried at the IETF ALARM-MIB arc (1.3.6.1.2.1.118.1.2.2.1.4, RFC 3877), with its six tokens exactly matching known_oids.SEVERITY_VOCAB. From v0.17.1 the appliance READS that word and places the alarm with provenance `standard` — it is the device's own statement about its own alarm, not an inference and not a claim about Huawei. Which alarmActiveEntry column `.4` is was not verified for this release: www.rfc-editor.org answers 403 to the build environment's proxy, and the read is keyed on the VALUE precisely so that it never depended on the answer.

ONE ALARM IN THE CUT PHASE DELIBERATELY CARRIES NO SEVERITY COLUMN (the rectifier fault at 1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.6.128.1.1.4.7). It stays UNPLACED and is counted as such, because a trap that says nothing about how serious it is gets no severity invented for it. It has no clear in the repair phase either, so it is still there when the demo settles — which is the point: a lab where everything is placed would not show you the half of the census that matters. Declaring a severity on its class is the one gesture that places it, and that is an operator's evidence in a way neither of the other two sources is.

hosts.role: GPON OLT, west end of the cut span
GPON OLT, east end of the cut span

steady.description: Nothing is broken. A flapping access port on olt-a, raised and cleared five seconds later, every twelve seconds — the most ordinary thing in a real NOC, and the reason the console is not empty before the cut. It uses the STANDARD linkDown/linkUp pair, which the appliance already knows (known_oids.CLEAR_PAIR_SEEDS), so it clears from the very first heartbeat and never leaves an alarm behind to hold the fibre-cut situation open after the repair. ifIndex 999 keeps it a different instance from the two span uplinks, so it is a distinct alarm rather than a duplicate of the cut.

events.role: a flapping access port goes down
…and comes back (bundled pair, clears with no learning)

cut.description: The span is cut. Both OLTs lose the uplink within a second of each other, then every ONU behind each one reports loss of signal and dying gasp. This is the storm the correlator has to collapse into one situation.

events.role: root: standard linkDown on the cut span (west end)
the far end of the same cut, seen from the other host
excessive bit error rate as the span degrades
the storm: every ONU behind olt-a reports loss of signal
the same storm behind the other host
an alarm that carries NO severity column, so the appliance must leave it unplaced (v0.17.1) — a rectifier fault on the same shelf, reported by a subsystem that never implemented ALARM-MIB

varbinds.value: rectifier module input voltage out of range

repair.description: The splice is done. The span comes up first — a standard linkUp, which the appliance pairs with linkDown out of the box — then the ONUs re-range. The ONU pairing is learned rather than bundled, so on the first two repairs those alarms stay active and from the third cut onward they clear.

events.role: clear: standard linkUp, the span is back (west end)
clear: the bit error rate is back inside spec (learned pair)
clear: the ONUs re-range behind olt-a (learned pair)
clear: the ONUs re-range behind olt-b (learned pair)
